subject: Post-demo: Omnicare latency & throughput benchmark scope
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@omnicare.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Priya Nanjiani <priya.n@omnicare.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 15:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-demo: Omnicare latency & throughput benchmarks

Hi Kimberly / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — helpful walkthrough. A few quick items we need to lock down before we share the evaluation with our infra team:

- Confirm you can run an apples-to-apples A/B against our current hyperscaler baseline (Bedrock + custom inference layer) for p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec at two slice sizes: 512-token conversational, and a heavier 2048-token document completion workload.
- We want results for: p50/p95/p99 latency, median tokens/sec per GPU, and overall throughput at target concurrency.
- Our peak concurrency target for the proof: 35-45 concurrent chat users (steady-state), with 5x short bursts for 1–2 minutes.
- Please include failure-mode behavior (fallbacks, retries) and how KV cache impacts p95/p99.

I attached our initial prompt samples and a short traffic profile. Can you confirm what Redwood needs from us (auth, sample keys, any specific prompt pre-processing) and an estimated ETA for the lab run?

Also copy of our decision criteria: cost per 1M tokens (estimate), p99 latency under 1s for 512 tokens (ideal), graceful fallback to smaller/cheaper model if capacity constrained.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of Machine Learning
Omnicare Labs
Attachments: omnicare_sample_prompts.csv, omnicare_traffic_profile.json
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@omnicare.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Omnicare latency & throughput benchmarks

Alex — great to meet you both. Quick reply with a concrete plan so we can get the lab scheduled.

Recap of ask (we captured):
- A/B head-to-head (Redwood hosted + Dedicated pool) vs your Bedrock baseline
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (per-GPU), overall throughput, and observed error/retry rates under burst
- Workloads: 512-token chat and 2048-token doc completion; concurrency profile ~40 concurrent users with 5x spikes
- Additional: KV cache influence, fallback policy behavior, and cost-estimate delta

Proposed Redwood lab matrix (attached as a draft):
- Test A: Redwood Hosted (curated model x quant profile) — 512 tokens, 40 concurrent, 10-minute steady run + 2-minute bursts
- Test B: Redwood Dedicated (N1 reserved) — same slice sizes
- Test C: Bedrock baseline (we will run on your provided Bedrock logs if you prefer; otherwise we run equivalent requests against your Bedrock account)
- Each test: 3 runs per slice, capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec per-GPU, backend CPU/GPU utilization, retry counts

Requirements from Omnicare to run:
1) Short list of representative prompts (you sent — thanks).
2) Access: either a temporary Bedrock API key so we can run the baseline from our lab, or a recent Bedrock log export we can replay.
3) A small corpus for the 2048-token workload (we can reuse your prompts) and the traffic profile json (attached).

ETA: If we get keys/logs by EOD Monday (Jan 12), we can run the initial sweep and share a preliminary readout by end-of-week Jan 16. Finalized runs + cost delta by Jan 20.

Next steps / action items:
- Omnicare: confirm which option for Bedrock baseline (key vs logs) and confirm the test concurrency shape.
- Redwood (me): finalize lab matrix and post the shared run plan in a Drive folder (link below).
- Quick sync — 30 minutes Tuesday Jan 13 to align the timeline and any IP/NDAs.

Drive folder (draft plan): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink
Attachments: redwood_lab_matrix_v1.xlsx

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Omnicare latency & throughput benchmarks

Kimberly — thanks, that plan looks good. Couple clarifications and one ask: 

Clarifications:
- We will provide a temporary Bedrock API key (expires in 7 days) — please confirm you’ll delete after the runs.
- For KV cache: our architecture currently stores short-term conversation state in a managed KV with 1–2 token-per-turn overhead; we want to see both cold-cache and warmed-cache runs.

Ask: can you include a small RPS sweep to determine the concurrency knee (tokens/sec per GPU vs increasing RPS) — we care about the point where adding traffic no longer increases tokens/sec linearly.

We attached a slightly more detailed traffic profile (bursts modeled). Also, please include any lightweight instrumentation hooks you need (trace-id header or custom request header) so we can correlate logs on our side.

We can do the Tuesday sync — Priya will send a calendar invite. Expect keys by Monday morning.

Alex
Attachments: omnicare_traffic_profile.json

Alex / Priya — got the Bedrock key this morning (thank you). Quick update and confirmed schedule: 

Confirmed scope:
- Tests: cold-cache vs warmed-cache, 512-token and 2048-token slices, RPS sweep to identify knee, p50/p95/p99 capture, tokens/sec per GPU, and error/retry profiles.
- Environments: Redwood Hosted (curated model v2q), Redwood Dedicated (reserved N1 pool), and Bedrock baseline (your provided key).
- Runs: 3 repeats per configuration; automated charting and a small evaluation harness that runs the same deterministic seed prompts to make the comparison reproducible.

Timeline (fixed):
- Jan 12–13: Run matrix + RPS sweep (engineering will run overnight jobs)
- Jan 14: Preliminary data dump and quick sync (30m) to review surprising deltas
- Jan 15–16: Targeted follow-ups (longer runs if we need to reduce variance)
- Jan 20: Final readout + cost delta and recommendation memo

Can you confirm:
1) Are you okay with us running the Bedrock baseline from our lab (we have your key) or do you want the runs executed from your VPC?
2) Any constraints on collecting full latency traces (we will redact PII and share aggregates only).

We attached the working lab matrix and will drop final run scripts into the Drive folder. I’ll block 30 minutes Jan 14 09:00 PT for the readout — Priya, please confirm if that works for you.

Attachments: redwood_lab_matrix_v1.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Best,
